title_ar: محبة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومحبة ما جاء به
title_en: Love of the Messenger of God, Peace and Blessings Be upon Him, and Love of What He Brought
body_ar:
بأي طريقة يحب الإنسان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم محبة كاملة ويحب كل ما جاء به؟

أن من أراد أن يحب رسول الله (ص) فعليه أن يتعرف عليه أولا، أن يعرف من هو رسول الله (ص)، فإذا درس الإنسان سيرته وشخصيته وحياته فلا بد أن يحبه حبا شديدا، ولذلك فإن أهل الأندلس لما ألف القاضي عياض رحمه الله كتاب الشفا في التعريف بحقوق المصطفى (ص) فقرأوه قالوا: لولا الشفا لما عرف المصطفى (ص)، فلا بد أن يتعرف الإنسان إلى النبي (ص) وأن يدرس سيرته، وحياته وشمائله حتى يحبه حبا شديدا، ثم بعد ذلك أن يتعود على هذه المحبة لعلمه أنها شرط لإيمانه كما قال النبي (ص): «لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى أكون أحب إليه من والده وولده والناس أجمعين» فلا بد أن يتدرب على محبته وإيثاره وتقديمه على كل من سواه.
body_en:
By what means does a person come to love the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, with a complete love, and to love everything he brought?

Whoever wishes to love the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, must first come to know him — to know who the Messenger of God is. If a person studies his biography (sīrah), his character and his life, he cannot but come to love him intensely. That is why, when Qadi ʿIyad, God have mercy on him, composed the book al-Shifāʾ fī l-taʿrīf bi-ḥuqūq al-Muṣṭafā ('The Cure: On Making Known the Rights of the Chosen One'), the people of Andalusia read it and said: 'Were it not for al-Shifāʾ, the Chosen One would not be known.' So a person must come to know the Prophet, and must study his biography, his life and his personal qualities (shamāʾil), until he loves him intensely. Then after that he should accustom himself to this love, knowing that it is a condition (sharṭ) of his faith (īmān), as the Prophet said: 'None of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child and all people.' So he must train himself in loving him, in giving him preference, and in putting him ahead of everyone besides him.

flags.context: the saying the Sheikh attributes to the people of Andalusia about Qadi ʿIyad's al-Shifāʾ
options: Were it not for al-Shifāʾ, the Chosen One would not be known
But for al-Shifāʾ, al-Muṣṭafā would not have been recognised
Without al-Shifāʾ, the Chosen One would have gone unknown
flags.note: The Arabic is a rhymed saying (al-Shifā / al-Muṣṭafā) and the rhyme cannot be carried into English without distorting the sense; it has been rendered as plain prose per the house rule against rhymed English. The saying is proverbial in the Maghrib; the Sheikh reports it of 'the people of Andalusia' and gives no source, and none has been supplied.

shamāʾil is a genre term as much as a common noun — the literature on the Prophet's physical description, manners and habits, of which al-Tirmidhi's al-Shamāʾil is the type. The Sheikh is listing three fields of study side by side (sīrah, life, shamāʾil), so the English should read as a field of study and not as a loose synonym for 'character', which he has already used in the previous sentence.

Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-21 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The source writes the eulogy after the Prophet's name sometimes in full (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and sometimes as the abbreviation (ص). Both are rendered in English as 'peace and blessings be upon him'; the abbreviation is preserved in body_ar.

The full title of Qadi ʿIyad's work is given in the source in a shortened form (كتاب الشفا في التعريف بحقوق المصطفى). It has been transliterated and an English rendering of the title supplied in brackets; the work itself is not named in English anywhere in the corpus yet, so a reviewer may wish to fix a standard form.
The hadith is quoted by the Sheikh without narrator, collection or grading, and none has been supplied.
